small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_OC tiles (e.g. BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_OC=128 num_warps=8, BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_OC=128 num_warps=4 stages=3) since OC=64 makes BLOCK_OC=64 use only 1 program in OC dim — try BLOCK_OC=64 with much larger BLOCK_N (e.g. 256/512) and num_warps=8 to increase parallelism per OC tile.
- K_REAL = 8*3*3 = 72 rounds up to BLOCK_K=128, wasting ~44% of the dot. Specialize on KH=KW=3 by unrolling kh/kw into an outer loop (BLOCK_K = IC=8, looped 9 times) so the dot is dense; this should dramatically cut wasted FLOPs.
- Try swizzled program ordering (group_size on pid_n) to improve L2 reuse of W tiles across adjacent spatial outputs.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a direct conv kernel that tiles over (OH, OW) spatial blocks instead of a flat N axis, so KH×KW input rows can be reused across the tile through a shared-memory cache; loop over (kh, kw) with BLOCK_K = IC (or padded to 16), eliminating the K-padding waste from rounding 72→128.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) input/weight layout so the K reduction axis (IC) is the contiguous dim — coalesced GEMM-K loads, and W can be laid out [KH,KW,IC,OC] for streaming.
- Persistent-CTA scheme: one program per (OC tile, spatial tile) iterating across batch, amortizing weight loads; fuse hardswish→relu in the epilogue (already doing this) and write NHWC output, transposing once at the end if the reference expects NCHW.
